Native R embedding, recurrence and nonlinear-dynamics visual diagnostics

etr_native_scientific_visualization.Rd

Eight Python-free native R descriptive graphics plotting the exact stored scientific geometry without automatic parameter tuning or mathematical estimator modification. These functions are experimental source-name analogues; they are not exact Matplotlib output contracts.

Plotting parameters

result

A corresponding native embedding-delay, FNN-dimension, recurrence-network, radius-profile, windowed-RQA, local-divergence, largest-Lyapunov or surrogate-nonlinearity diagnostic result.

normalized

Use degree normalized by source node count.

metrics

Distinct available numeric windowed-RQA columns.

bins

Integer histogram-break count (>=2) for base R plotting. In the explicit source-boundary mode, must be a Python-style integer within the native finite 10000-bin safety limit.

python_boundary_mode

If TRUE, reproduce exact finite NumPy equal-width integer-bin edges and left-inclusive counts for the surrogate-nonlinearity histogram. FALSE retains the existing base R histogram interpretation and validation.

crossings

One-dimensional native Poincare crossing result with at least two observed crossings.

fit

Optional compatible one-dimensional native local affine map.

...

Additional native plotting parameters.

Value

Each function draws into the active R graphics device and returns the plotted numeric geometry invisibly. Return classes and graphics devices are not Matplotlib Axes. The source-boundary mode of etr_plot_surrogate_nonlinearity() aligns NumPy integer-bin histogram geometry for finite surrogate samples, but all other graphics and native R result classes retain their native behavior.

Details

The visualisations preserve the declared physical-time/lag coordinates, source sample-index semantics, ordered diagnostic tables, and recorded fit intervals. All source-name parity ledger entries remain full-contract certification pending: graphical-backend return objects are an explicit known divergence. These plots are descriptive and do not provide causal inference, chaos classification, or calibrated confidence by themselves.
